title: Let a huge invoice give its memory back

blocks.text: Each invoice-export worker formats every invoice in one `StringBuilder` of its own, kept in `ScratchBuffer`, and the workers live as long as the service. Once a month a customer's invoice runs to tens of thousands of lines. Since then, monitoring shows the export service's heap staying high for weeks, and the heap dump finds each worker holding a buffer of several hundred kilobytes, all of it empty.

Write `acquire()` in `src/main/java/practice/ScratchBuffer.java`. When you're done, each invoice starts from an empty builder; after a huge invoice the worker holds no more than `KEEP_LIMIT` characters of room; and ordinary invoices, including the next one after a huge one, start with `NORMAL_CAPACITY` ready. About five lines.

cases.says: each formatted invoice holds its own rows and nothing left from the one before
a run of ordinary invoices leaves the worker with the room it started with
after a huge invoice, the worker holds no more than the keep limit once the next invoice starts
after a huge invoice, the next ordinary invoice still finds the normal room ready rather than growing from nothing

origin.section: setLength(0) Empties a Builder and Keeps Its Array

concepts: setLength(0) empties a builder but keeps its array, so a reused builder holds its largest size; trimToSize() gives it back but leaves no room.
